sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. April 14, 2025 announcement explicitly launches GPT-4.1, mini and nano, with separate nano evaluations. Describes nano as small, fast and inexpensive but gives neither a nominal total nor an active parameter count, and no named counted base-model lineage.

sources.title: GPT-4.1 nano model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh complete Markdown fetched October 27, 2026. Exact nano alias defaults to gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14, with text/image input, text output, 1,047,576 context and supported features including prompt_caching and fine_tuning. Neither nominal total nor active parameters is stated. Alias and snapshot are shut down.

sources.title: API deprecations: legacy GPT model snapshots
sources.evidence: Exact alias gpt-4.1-nano and snapshot gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 are listed with October 23, 2026 shutdown. This differs from the January 2027 schedule for full GPT-4.1 and mini.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown explains PDF processing for vision-capable models: extracted text plus page images. Read with the exact nano page confirming file uploads, image input and the supported API endpoints; this establishes an API input format, not a separate native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves intellectual-property rights in the service; customers receive limited usage rights rather than ownership. Supports descriptive Proprietary classification for the hosted API model.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: Complete indexed primary article read after direct requests timed out or returned 403. August 5, 2025 announcement identifies gpt-oss as the first open-weight language models since GPT-2, consistent with the earlier API-only nano release.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card, August 13, 2025 revision
sources.evidence: Fresh full 55-page PDF fetched October 27, 2026 and searched for parameter, model-size, billion/million and nano references. Table 1 names GPT-4.1-nano as the predecessor of gpt-5-thinking-nano; this is a successor mapping, not a counted shared-base declaration. No total or active nano count is supplied.

sources.title: Supervised fine-tuning
sources.evidence: Fresh complete supervised-fine-tuning Markdown fetched October 27, 2026. Identifies gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 as a historical fine-tuning base and records its shutdown. Training examples and hyperparameters give no nominal model total, active count or link to a named base with published size.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: February 18, 2026 OpenAI guide describes pre-GPT-5.6 API prompt caching through Transformer attention layers and key/value tensors. Although its examples name full GPT-4.1 rather than nano, the exact nano model documentation independently lists prompt_caching support; combining that explicit support with the documented mechanism supports a broad operational architecture inference, not complete block structure or routing.

sources.title: Fine-grained Confidence Estimation for Spurious Correctness Detection in Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Fresh full original paper read October 27, 2026. Section 4.3 identifies the exact GPT-4.1-nano 2025-04-14 snapshot; footnote 5 explicitly says GPT-4.1 variant parameter counts are not publicly disclosed. Independent research corroboration, not an OpenAI specification; supplies no active count.

sources.title: Directed Attention is All You Need: Profiling Style from Limited Text Data
sources.evidence: Fresh full original paper read and Table 7 on PDF page 14 visually inspected October 27, 2026. Exact openai/gpt-4.1-nano row says Size (B) 7.0; the asterisk identifies OpenRouter access only. The paper provides no provenance or count-estimation method for this closed-model size, and no active-parameter column. Reject the unsupported 7B claim rather than promoting it to a model specification.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity, v2
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched complete July 5, 2026 v2 PDF read October 27; also reopened the original v1 HTML. Abstract and methodology explicitly estimate coarse effective knowledge capacity using calibration against open models. The exact gpt-4.1-nano row leaves known size blank. Neither these capacity estimates nor hallucination-similarity relationships establish a published total, an active-count convention, or a named developer-confirmed base lineage.

family.note: Nano belongs to the named GPT-4.1 family; replace the cross-generation gpt-nano bucket.

release_date.note: Dated announcement explicitly launches nano in the API; later fine-tuning support is a different event.

open_weights.note: API-only launch and later open-weight release history support closed weights; hosted fine-tuning is not weight distribution.

license.note: Descriptive classification of service access under commercial terms, not an SPDX weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit found no developer-published nominal total or explicit lineage to a counted base in the release, exact model documentation, fine-tuning guide or later GPT-5 card. The original SIGTURK paper lists 7.0B without source or measurement provenance; IKP estimates effective knowledge capacity, not the model specification. Neither supports replacing null.

active_parameters_b.note: Checked separately for active/activated-parameter disclosures and later original research comparisons. No explicit active-count convention for exact GPT-4.1 nano was found. SIGTURK labels only Size (B), and IKP studies capacity rather than nano parameter participation; neither supplies an active count. Do not infer equality from total size, price, product tier or successor models.

architecture.note: Cross-source operational inference: exact nano documentation explicitly supports prompt_caching, and OpenAI describes the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 mechanism as Transformer attention and key/value caching. This establishes a Transformer attention stack, not exclusively Transformer layers, a complete block inventory, dense/MoE routing or parameter counts. It does not depend on transferring the full GPT-4.1 table row.

context_window.note: Exact model context; 32,768 output ceiling is separate. This records documented model capacity rather than current endpoint operation.

modalities.note: Text/image to text is explicit. PDF is an API file format added by combining exact nano file-upload/vision support with the official PDF processing rule; the API supplies extracted text and page images.

reasoning.note: The exact nano documentation explicitly describes operation without a reasoning step; this classification does not mean inability to solve reasoning tasks.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation supports function calling, independently corroborated by nano launch evaluations. Historical capability, not a claim of live availability.

description.value: Non-reasoning GPT-4.1 variant with text and image input, text output, and function calling.
description.note: Replace promotional size and throughput language with documented behavior.

patch.notes: Release date is the April 14, 2025 API launch. The last documented default snapshot is gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14; OpenAI lists both it and the alias as shut down on October 23, 2026. Specifications describe the historical model. PDF denotes API file input processed as extracted text and page images. Explicit nano prompt-caching support and OpenAI's documented pre-GPT-5.6 caching mechanism support a broad Transformer-attention inference. Complete structure and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. No supported total or active parameter count was found; an unsourced 7B research-table entry and effective-capacity estimates do not establish model specifications.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after reopening OpenAI disclosures and checking later original research. Reject the unsourced 7B comparison-table claim and IKP effective-capacity estimates as specification evidence. Preserve all other 12 field assessments and the earlier family, license, PDF-input, description and broad Transformer-attention corrections.
